input.rationale: Interpret the successor receipt, correct the knowledge it changes and register the remaining applicability question. The isolating run confirmed the follower-local consequence with a single re-synchronized replica (its endpoint flips and its decided-log read loses all six elements, receipt 9125b6a531234e7d9d2fa8cbb817df63 event 35) while the leader stayed consistent (event 37), which shows the leader's decision at the phantom index 7 requires a write quorum of inflated reports, as reproduced in events 22-24 of the same receipt and in the earlier receipt. The interpretation now covers both receipts with the same-run controls, a limitation narrows the consequence to index accounting and readability because the sealed configuration admits no further entries, the index-shift behavior is generalized to both observed decided-index positions, two behaviors/facts are added (the decision rule that ignores the leader's own log bound, and the sourced applicability condition including its independence from the snapshot option), and one gap is registered for the snapshot branch and for a new leader applying a follower's LogSync.

investigations.discriminator: Whether a snapshot-enabled configuration reproduces the inflation or the sourced branch difference prevents it, and whether a new leader that already decided the StopSign is inflated when it syncs from a follower at a higher accepted round (the candidate's own decided index becomes sync_idx).

knowledge.statement: On a replica that already holds the accepted StopSign, applying an AcceptSync whose LogSync carries that StopSign leaves the stored log unchanged while the reported accepted index rises by one; the replica's read of the StopSign's previous index (5) then returns None, its read of index 6 returns the StopSign, and read_decided_suffix(0) returns a decided log that omits the five entries: one element (the StopSign) when the replica's decided index has been pushed past the StopSign's index, and an empty list when its decided index still stops at that index.
knowledge.conditions: Three-node cluster, five decided entries plus a StopSign, no snapshots (NoSnapshot), default batch size, re-synchronization triggered by a follower's public reconnected() call after the StopSign was accepted and decided. Both variants were observed: two followers re-synchronize (receipt 8b314551f1e049fcbf73a358f8ddf2c8 events 22, 23 with a one-element decided read; receipt 9125b6a531234e7d9d2fa8cbb817df63 events 22, 23) and only one follower re-synchronizes (receipt 9125b6a531234e7d9d2fa8cbb817df63 event 35 with an empty decided read and decided index 6), always against the same replica's pre-resynchronization state (6/6, six-element read) and the no-reconnect control.

knowledge.assertion: sync_log adds the StopSign carried by LogSync on top of sync_idx + suffix.len()

knowledge.changed_premise: Generalizes the decided-log read effect from one observed decided-index position to both observed positions: with a quorum of inflated reports the leader's phantom decision pushes the replica's decided index past the StopSign index and the read keeps the StopSign alone, while with a single inflated report the decided index stays at the StopSign index and the read returns an empty list.

knowledge.statement: The inflated accepted index follows from the resume point being compared against the index the StopSign occupies in the receiving replica's accounting: sync_log computes accepted_idx = LogSync.sync_idx + LogSync.suffix.len() and adds one for a carried StopSign, while the StopSign occupies the index accepted_idx - 1 and the sender attaches it without shifting sync_idx. The condition is therefore sync_idx + suffix.len() >= the StopSign's index, and it does not depend on the snapshot option: the no-snapshot branch passes the caller's common_prefix_idx unchanged (the follower's accepted index, which already counts the StopSign), whereas the snapshot branch passes the compacted index returned by create_diff_snapshot, which is derived from get_decided_idx_without_stopsign and therefore excludes the StopSign.
knowledge.conditions: Holds for any LogSync whose stopsign is Some; the snapshot branch is only entered when T::Snapshot::use_snapshots() is true and the sender's decided index exceeds common_prefix_idx. Sourced from the captured snapshot; the observed inflation (receipts 8b314551f1e049fcbf73a358f8ddf2c8 and 9125b6a531234e7d9d2fa8cbb817df63) is a no-snapshot instance of the condition and no snapshot-enabled execution has been run.

knowledge.statement: A leader in the accept phase accepts a decision at the accepted index reported by any matching-ballot Accepted message: it records that index for the sender, and if the index exceeds its own decided index and a write quorum of recorded accepted indexes covers it, it sets its decided index to exactly that reported index, without comparing it against the length of its own log or against its own accepted index.
knowledge.conditions: Leader role in Phase::Accept with a matching ballot; the recorded accepted indexes include the leader's own slot as it was last written by its own accept handling. Observed: with two inflated reports the leader reported decided index 7 while holding six indices and its own accepted index stayed 6 (receipt 8b314551f1e049fcbf73a358f8ddf2c8 event 24; reproduced in receipt 9125b6a531234e7d9d2fa8cbb817df63 event 24), while with a single inflated report no write quorum was reached and the leader stayed at 6/6 (receipt 9125b6a531234e7d9d2fa8cbb817df63 event 37).

gaps.question: Does the same inflation occur when T::Snapshot::use_snapshots() is true (the snapshot branch is not entered in the observed scenario because the sender's decided index equals the resume point), and can a leader's own accepted index be inflated when handle_majority_promises applies a follower's LogSync whose stopsign is Some and whose sync_idx already covers the StopSign?

interpretations.rationale: The isolating successor run confirms and narrows the account. Receipt 9125b6a531234e7d9d2fa8cbb817df63 (same harness lineage, third case added; all three tests passed) showed: with only node 1 re-synchronized, node 1 alone ended at accepted 7 over the same six indices of content, decided 6, so its own reported reconfiguration endpoint flipped from true to false, its read of the StopSign's index 5 returned None while its read of index 6 returned the StopSign, and its decided-log read from 0 returned an empty list where it had returned six elements before (event 35); nodes 2 and 3 stayed at 6/6 with a six-element decided read and is_reconfigured true (events 36, 37). That separates the two consequences: the follower-local inflation and endpoint/read corruption need only one re-synchronized replica, while the leader's decision at index 7 requires a write quorum of inflated reports (the two-follower case, event 24 in both receipts). The comparisons match: on the single case, comparisons 3-6 (node 1 reports the reconfiguration as decided; its decided index is covered by the entries it holds; its StopSign stays at index 5; its decided log keeps six elements) were violated at index 35, while comparisons 7-8 (the leader still reports the reconfiguration as decided and stays consistent) hold at index 37; comparison 2 holds the baseline that index 6 held no StopSign before the re-synchronization (index 19). The declared defect stands: a public reconnected() call on a replica that has accepted the configuration's StopSign corrupts that replica's index accounting, hides the configuration transition from the user, and - with a write quorum of such reports - makes the leader declare a decided index past every entry it holds, after which the leader itself no longer reports the reconfiguration as decided and cannot read its decided log at all.

knowledge.assertion: sync_log double-counts the StopSign when the resumed prefix already contains it
a re-synchronized replica's decided log read loses the entries
the condition is the resume point covering the StopSign's index
the leader decides the reported accepted index without bounding it to its own log

counterevidence: The no-reconnect control of the same execution kept every endpoint consistent (accepted 6, decided 6, is_reconfigured true, six-element decided read; receipt 8b314551f1e049fcbf73a358f8ddf2c8 events 9-11 and the control case of the successor run), so the deviation is caused by the re-established-connection path rather than by the reconfiguration, the harness or the reading.

The single-replica case limits the leader-side consequence: one inflated report did not reach a write quorum, so the leader kept decided 6 with is_reconfigured true (receipt 9125b6a531234e7d9d2fa8cbb817df63 event 37); the decision at the phantom index therefore requires a write quorum of inflated reports (both followers of a three-node cluster) within one term.

The documented reconfiguration flow (agent-source/docs/omnipaxos/reconfiguration.md 25-34) expects the user to start a new instance once a node observes LogEntry::StopSign(ss, true), so a user who stops the old instance immediately narrows the user-facing window; the defect still bites the leader, which never observes the decision after the corruption, and any replica whose log is read while its old instance still runs.

The leader's phantom decision is inferred from its reported state (decided 7 with accepted 6 and six indices of content) plus the followers' inflated 7; the internal accepted-index vector was not sampled, so which reports formed the quorum rests on the source rule that any matching-ballot Accepted index counts, not on a direct trace.
limitations: No snapshot-enabled execution has been run; the sourced applicability fact says the snapshot branch computes sync_idx without the StopSign, so the defect is not specific to NoSnapshot entries, but that branch was not exercised.

Messages were delivered in FIFO order without loss and without tick()-driven timers, so the re-established-connection call is the only recovery trigger exercised; a loss-triggered re-synchronization path that produces the same resume point is untested.

The consequence is bounded by the sealed configuration: after the StopSign is accepted no further entries can be accepted, so the phantom decided index carries no value and no value can be mis-assigned; the demonstrated effects are the corrupted index accounting, the unreadable or blank decided log, and the lost reconfiguration endpoint rather than divergent values.

All three nodes used in-memory storage; persistence across a restart and other storages' behaviour on out-of-range reads (a storage-implementer responsibility per the Storage trait) were not exercised.
Only three-node clusters with a single uninterrupted term were exercised; larger clusters and repeated leader changes around the re-synchronization were not.

interpretations.rationale: Source reading of the re-synchronization path (PrepareReq -> Prepare -> Promise -> AcceptSync -> Accepted) suggests that a replica which has accepted the StopSign gets its accepted index inflated by one when it is re-synchronized at the same ballot: in handle_promise_accept the leader calls send_accsync, whose first branch uses the follower's own accepted index as the valid prefix (leader.rs 150-191), and that index already includes the StopSign because set_stopsign adds it (internal_storage.rs 503-512). create_log_sync then reports that index as LogSync.sync_idx with the sender's StopSign attached, and sync_log adds the StopSign once more, so the follower's accepted index ends at prefix + suffix + 1 while its decided index is the AcceptSync's decided index (internal_storage.rs 313-360). The follower then reports that inflated index in Accepted (follower.rs 112-126), and the leader's decision rule accepts any incoming accepted index whose count reaches a write quorum (leader.rs 316-345), so a write quorum of inflated reports would set the leader's decided index past the entries it holds. Both endpoints this reading endangers are public: is_reconfigured() is gated on stopsign_is_decided() (mod.rs 284-290, state_cache.rs 123-126), the bool of LogEntry::StopSign is documented as 'the reconfiguration has been decided' (util.rs 277-279), and the documented user flow reads the decided suffix and switches configuration only on StopSign(.., true) (reconfiguration.md 25-34). The final judgment is left unresolved until the two-case execution samples the endpoints; the reading also predicts that a fresh or lagging follower, whose prefix does not yet contain the StopSign, is unaffected. Counterevidence and limits: the reconfiguration documentation tells the user to start a new instance once the StopSign is observed as decided, so the affected window is an old instance that keeps running after (or while) it observes the decision and then re-synchronizes; the accounting is correct whenever sync_idx stays at or below the StopSign's own index, which covers the normal catch-up path; the account rests on static reading of the read() combination paths and of MemoryStorage's empty-range behaviour, not on an executed observation.

Confirmed by execution: the re-synchronization of a replica that already accepted its configuration's StopSign inflates its reported accepted index by one, and a write quorum of such reports makes the leader decide an index past every entry it holds. Receipt 8b314551f1e049fcbf73a358f8ddf2c8, two cases in one run over three real OmniPaxos instances with MemoryStorage (events: 19,20,21 = after the StopSign was decided on all three nodes; 22,23 = the two re-synchronized followers; 24 = the leader; 9,10,11 = the identical prefix without reconnected()). Before the re-synchronization all three nodes reported accepted 6, decided 6, is_reconfigured true, read(5) = StopSign with decided = true, and read_decided_suffix(0) = six elements. After both followers called reconnected(3): node 1 and node 2 reported accepted 7 over the same six indices of content, their read(5) returned None (the StopSign is now placed at index 6 by the internal index-type rule), and their decided-log read from 0 returned a single element (the StopSign), so the five decided entries disappeared from the readable decided log while is_reconfigured stayed true; node 3 (leader) reported decided 7 with accepted 6, is_reconfigured false where it had been true, read(5) = StopSign with decided = false, and read_decided_suffix(0) = None, i.e. the user on the leader can no longer read the decided log at all and never observes the reconfiguration as complete. The declared comparisons match this reading: comparison 2 (leader reports the reconfiguration as decided) violated at index 24, comparison 3 (decided index covered by entries held) violated at index 24, comparison 4 (leader's decided log readable from 0) violated at index 24, comparison 5 (re-synchronized follower's decided log still has the five entries plus the StopSign) violated at indices 22 and 23, while comparisons 0 and 1 (the same predicates before the reconnection, indices 19-21) and comparisons 6 and 7 (the no-reconnect control, indices 9-11) hold, which attributes the change to the re-synchronization rather than to the reconfiguration or to the sampling.

27bf7fc0875c4342966bd3dc15df80ec-gap-0.explanation: The legitimate producer path was observed end to end: node 1 and node 2 each called the public reconnected(3) after the StopSign had been accepted and decided; reconnected() sets the follower to Phase::Recover and sends PrepareReq with its current promise (agent-source/omnipaxos/src/sequence_paxos/mod.rs 343-357); the leader in Phase::Accept handles it via handle_preparereq, resets the follower's promise state and re-sends Prepare (leader.rs 66-74); the follower, now in Phase::Recover with its promise equal to the Prepare's ballot, re-promises with accepted_idx = 6, an index that already counts its stored StopSign (follower.rs 13-51, internal_storage.rs 503-512); handle_promise_accept then calls send_accsync (leader.rs 301-314), and because the promise's accepted round equals the leader's current ballot, send_accsync takes its first branch and uses the follower's own accepted index as the valid prefix (leader.rs 150-191), producing LogSync{sync_idx: 6, suffix: [], stopsign: Some} from create_log_sync (mod.rs 405-432); sync_log then adds the StopSign once more (internal_storage.rs 313-360). Receipt 8b314551f1e049fcbf73a358f8ddf2c8 confirms the outcome on the sampled endpoints (events 22 and 23).

knowledge.statement: On a replica that already holds the accepted StopSign, applying an AcceptSync whose LogSync carries that StopSign leaves the stored log unchanged while the reported accepted index rises by one; the replica's read of the StopSign's previous index (5) then returns None, its read of index 6 returns the StopSign, and read_decided_suffix(0) returns a decided log that omits the five entries: one element (the StopSign) when the replica's decided index has been pushed past the StopSign's index, and an empty list when its decided index still stops at that index.
knowledge.conditions: Three-node cluster, five decided entries plus a StopSign, no snapshots (NoSnapshot), default batch size, re-synchronization triggered by a follower's public reconnected() call after the StopSign was accepted and decided. Both variants were observed: two followers re-synchronize (receipt 8b314551f1e049fcbf73a358f8ddf2c8 events 22, 23 with a one-element decided read; receipt 9125b6a531234e7d9d2fa8cbb817df63 events 22, 23) and only one follower re-synchronizes (receipt 9125b6a531234e7d9d2fa8cbb817df63 event 35 with an empty decided read and decided index 6), always against the same replica's pre-resynchronization state (6/6, six-element read) and the no-reconnect control.

history.statement: On a replica that already holds the accepted StopSign, applying an AcceptSync whose LogSync carries that StopSign leaves the stored log unchanged while the reported accepted index rises by one; the replica's read of the StopSign's previous index (5) then returns None, its read of the next index (6) returns the StopSign, and read_decided_suffix(0) returns a decided log of one element (the StopSign) rather than the six elements it returned before, because the internal index-type decision places the StopSign at accepted_idx - 1.
history.conditions: Three-node cluster, five decided entries plus a StopSign, no snapshots (NoSnapshot), default batch size, re-synchronization triggered by a follower's public reconnected() call after the StopSign was accepted and decided; observed on node 1 and node 2 in receipt 8b314551f1e049fcbf73a358f8ddf2c8 (events 22, 23) against their own pre-resynchronization state (events 19, 20) and the no-reconnect control (events 10, 11).

knowledge.assertion: sync_log adds the StopSign carried by LogSync on top of sync_idx + suffix.len()

history.correction: Generalizes the decided-log read effect from one observed decided-index position to both observed positions: with a quorum of inflated reports the leader's phantom decision pushes the replica's decided index past the StopSign index and the read keeps the StopSign alone, while with a single inflated report the decided index stays at the StopSign index and the read returns an empty list.

knowledge.statement: The inflated accepted index follows from the resume point being compared against the index the StopSign occupies in the receiving replica's accounting: sync_log computes accepted_idx = LogSync.sync_idx + LogSync.suffix.len() and adds one for a carried StopSign, while the StopSign occupies the index accepted_idx - 1 and the sender attaches it without shifting sync_idx. The condition is therefore sync_idx + suffix.len() >= the StopSign's index, and it does not depend on the snapshot option: the no-snapshot branch passes the caller's common_prefix_idx unchanged (the follower's accepted index, which already counts the StopSign), whereas the snapshot branch passes the compacted index returned by create_diff_snapshot, which is derived from get_decided_idx_without_stopsign and therefore excludes the StopSign.
knowledge.conditions: Holds for any LogSync whose stopsign is Some; the snapshot branch is only entered when T::Snapshot::use_snapshots() is true and the sender's decided index exceeds common_prefix_idx. Sourced from the captured snapshot; the observed inflation (receipts 8b314551f1e049fcbf73a358f8ddf2c8 and 9125b6a531234e7d9d2fa8cbb817df63) is a no-snapshot instance of the condition and no snapshot-enabled execution has been run.

knowledge.statement: A leader in the accept phase accepts a decision at the accepted index reported by any matching-ballot Accepted message: it records that index for the sender, and if the index exceeds its own decided index and a write quorum of recorded accepted indexes covers it, it sets its decided index to exactly that reported index, without comparing it against the length of its own log or against its own accepted index.
knowledge.conditions: Leader role in Phase::Accept with a matching ballot; the recorded accepted indexes include the leader's own slot as it was last written by its own accept handling. Observed: with two inflated reports the leader reported decided index 7 while holding six indices and its own accepted index stayed 6 (receipt 8b314551f1e049fcbf73a358f8ddf2c8 event 24; reproduced in receipt 9125b6a531234e7d9d2fa8cbb817df63 event 24), while with a single inflated report no write quorum was reached and the leader stayed at 6/6 (receipt 9125b6a531234e7d9d2fa8cbb817df63 event 37).

interpretations.rationale: Source reading of the re-synchronization path (PrepareReq -> Prepare -> Promise -> AcceptSync -> Accepted) suggests that a replica which has accepted the StopSign gets its accepted index inflated by one when it is re-synchronized at the same ballot: in handle_promise_accept the leader calls send_accsync, whose first branch uses the follower's own accepted index as the valid prefix (leader.rs 150-191), and that index already includes the StopSign because set_stopsign adds it (internal_storage.rs 503-512). create_log_sync then reports that index as LogSync.sync_idx with the sender's StopSign attached, and sync_log adds the StopSign once more, so the follower's accepted index ends at prefix + suffix + 1 while its decided index is the AcceptSync's decided index (internal_storage.rs 313-360). The follower then reports that inflated index in Accepted (follower.rs 112-126), and the leader's decision rule accepts any incoming accepted index whose count reaches a write quorum (leader.rs 316-345), so a write quorum of inflated reports would set the leader's decided index past the entries it holds. Both endpoints this reading endangers are public: is_reconfigured() is gated on stopsign_is_decided() (mod.rs 284-290, state_cache.rs 123-126), the bool of LogEntry::StopSign is documented as 'the reconfiguration has been decided' (util.rs 277-279), and the documented user flow reads the decided suffix and switches configuration only on StopSign(.., true) (reconfiguration.md 25-34). The final judgment is left unresolved until the two-case execution samples the endpoints; the reading also predicts that a fresh or lagging follower, whose prefix does not yet contain the StopSign, is unaffected. Counterevidence and limits: the reconfiguration documentation tells the user to start a new instance once the StopSign is observed as decided, so the affected window is an old instance that keeps running after (or while) it observes the decision and then re-synchronizes; the accounting is correct whenever sync_idx stays at or below the StopSign's own index, which covers the normal catch-up path; the account rests on static reading of the read() combination paths and of MemoryStorage's empty-range behaviour, not on an executed observation.

Confirmed by execution: the re-synchronization of a replica that already accepted its configuration's StopSign inflates its reported accepted index by one, and a write quorum of such reports makes the leader decide an index past every entry it holds. Receipt 8b314551f1e049fcbf73a358f8ddf2c8, two cases in one run over three real OmniPaxos instances with MemoryStorage (events: 19,20,21 = after the StopSign was decided on all three nodes; 22,23 = the two re-synchronized followers; 24 = the leader; 9,10,11 = the identical prefix without reconnected()). Before the re-synchronization all three nodes reported accepted 6, decided 6, is_reconfigured true, read(5) = StopSign with decided = true, and read_decided_suffix(0) = six elements. After both followers called reconnected(3): node 1 and node 2 reported accepted 7 over the same six indices of content, their read(5) returned None (the StopSign is now placed at index 6 by the internal index-type rule), and their decided-log read from 0 returned a single element (the StopSign), so the five decided entries disappeared from the readable decided log while is_reconfigured stayed true; node 3 (leader) reported decided 7 with accepted 6, is_reconfigured false where it had been true, read(5) = StopSign with decided = false, and read_decided_suffix(0) = None, i.e. the user on the leader can no longer read the decided log at all and never observes the reconfiguration as complete. The declared comparisons match this reading: comparison 2 (leader reports the reconfiguration as decided) violated at index 24, comparison 3 (decided index covered by entries held) violated at index 24, comparison 4 (leader's decided log readable from 0) violated at index 24, comparison 5 (re-synchronized follower's decided log still has the five entries plus the StopSign) violated at indices 22 and 23, while comparisons 0 and 1 (the same predicates before the reconnection, indices 19-21) and comparisons 6 and 7 (the no-reconnect control, indices 9-11) hold, which attributes the change to the re-synchronization rather than to the reconfiguration or to the sampling.

27bf7fc0875c4342966bd3dc15df80ec-gap-0.explanation: The legitimate producer path was observed end to end: node 1 and node 2 each called the public reconnected(3) after the StopSign had been accepted and decided; reconnected() sets the follower to Phase::Recover and sends PrepareReq with its current promise (agent-source/omnipaxos/src/sequence_paxos/mod.rs 343-357); the leader in Phase::Accept handles it via handle_preparereq, resets the follower's promise state and re-sends Prepare (leader.rs 66-74); the follower, now in Phase::Recover with its promise equal to the Prepare's ballot, re-promises with accepted_idx = 6, an index that already counts its stored StopSign (follower.rs 13-51, internal_storage.rs 503-512); handle_promise_accept then calls send_accsync (leader.rs 301-314), and because the promise's accepted round equals the leader's current ballot, send_accsync takes its first branch and uses the follower's own accepted index as the valid prefix (leader.rs 150-191), producing LogSync{sync_idx: 6, suffix: [], stopsign: Some} from create_log_sync (mod.rs 405-432); sync_log then adds the StopSign once more (internal_storage.rs 313-360). Receipt 8b314551f1e049fcbf73a358f8ddf2c8 confirms the outcome on the sampled endpoints (events 22 and 23).

knowledge.assertion: sync_log double-counts the StopSign when the resumed prefix already contains it
a re-synchronized replica's decided log read shrinks to the StopSign alone

counterevidence: The no-reconnect control case of the same execution kept every endpoint consistent (accepted 6, decided 6, is_reconfigured true, six-element decided read at indices 9-11), so the deviation is attributable to the re-established-connection path and not to the reconfiguration, to the harness, or to reading the log.

The documented user flow for reconfiguration (agent-source/docs/omnipaxos/reconfiguration.md 25-34) expects the user to start a new instance once a node observes LogEntry::StopSign(ss, true); a user who stops the old instance immediately limits the user-facing window, but does not remove the defect: the leader of the same run never observes the StopSign as decided after the corruption (is_reconfigured false, decided log unreadable), and the two followers keep reporting the reconfiguration as decided while their decided log silently loses the five decided entries.

The leader's phantom decision is inferred from its own reported state (decided 7 with accepted 6 and six indices of content) plus the two followers' inflated 7; the internal accepted-index vector was not sampled, so the assignment of which reports formed the quorum rests on the source rule (handle_accepted decides any incoming accepted index reaching a write quorum) rather than on a direct trace of that vector.
limitations: No snapshots (NoSnapshot entries) and default batch size 1: whether the snapshot-enabled branch of create_log_sync inflates the same way is untested.

Messages were delivered in FIFO order without loss and without tick()-driven timers, so the re-established-connection call is the only recovery trigger exercised; loss-triggered re-synchronization is untested.

All three nodes used in-memory storage; persistence across a restart and the behaviour of other storages on out-of-range reads (a storage-implementer responsibility per the Storage trait) were not exercised.

The re-synchronization needed two followers of a three-node cluster to inflate for the leader to decide the phantom index 7; the single-replica case is targeted by the successor experiment submitted with this update.

interpretations.rationale: The isolating successor run confirms and narrows the account. Receipt 9125b6a531234e7d9d2fa8cbb817df63 (same harness lineage, third case added; all three tests passed) showed: with only node 1 re-synchronized, node 1 alone ended at accepted 7 over the same six indices of content, decided 6, so its own reported reconfiguration endpoint flipped from true to false, its read of the StopSign's index 5 returned None while its read of index 6 returned the StopSign, and its decided-log read from 0 returned an empty list where it had returned six elements before (event 35); nodes 2 and 3 stayed at 6/6 with a six-element decided read and is_reconfigured true (events 36, 37). That separates the two consequences: the follower-local inflation and endpoint/read corruption need only one re-synchronized replica, while the leader's decision at index 7 requires a write quorum of inflated reports (the two-follower case, event 24 in both receipts). The comparisons match: on the single case, comparisons 3-6 (node 1 reports the reconfiguration as decided; its decided index is covered by the entries it holds; its StopSign stays at index 5; its decided log keeps six elements) were violated at index 35, while comparisons 7-8 (the leader still reports the reconfiguration as decided and stays consistent) hold at index 37; comparison 2 holds the baseline that index 6 held no StopSign before the re-synchronization (index 19). The declared defect stands: a public reconnected() call on a replica that has accepted the configuration's StopSign corrupts that replica's index accounting, hides the configuration transition from the user, and - with a write quorum of such reports - makes the leader declare a decided index past every entry it holds, after which the leader itself no longer reports the reconfiguration as decided and cannot read its decided log at all.

a re-synchronized replica's decided log read loses the entries
the condition is the resume point covering the StopSign's index
the leader decides the reported accepted index without bounding it to its own log

counterevidence: The no-reconnect control of the same execution kept every endpoint consistent (accepted 6, decided 6, is_reconfigured true, six-element decided read; receipt 8b314551f1e049fcbf73a358f8ddf2c8 events 9-11 and the control case of the successor run), so the deviation is caused by the re-established-connection path rather than by the reconfiguration, the harness or the reading.

The single-replica case limits the leader-side consequence: one inflated report did not reach a write quorum, so the leader kept decided 6 with is_reconfigured true (receipt 9125b6a531234e7d9d2fa8cbb817df63 event 37); the decision at the phantom index therefore requires a write quorum of inflated reports (both followers of a three-node cluster) within one term.

The documented reconfiguration flow (agent-source/docs/omnipaxos/reconfiguration.md 25-34) expects the user to start a new instance once a node observes LogEntry::StopSign(ss, true), so a user who stops the old instance immediately narrows the user-facing window; the defect still bites the leader, which never observes the decision after the corruption, and any replica whose log is read while its old instance still runs.

The leader's phantom decision is inferred from its reported state (decided 7 with accepted 6 and six indices of content) plus the followers' inflated 7; the internal accepted-index vector was not sampled, so which reports formed the quorum rests on the source rule that any matching-ballot Accepted index counts, not on a direct trace.
limitations: No snapshot-enabled execution has been run; the sourced applicability fact says the snapshot branch computes sync_idx without the StopSign, so the defect is not specific to NoSnapshot entries, but that branch was not exercised.

Messages were delivered in FIFO order without loss and without tick()-driven timers, so the re-established-connection call is the only recovery trigger exercised; a loss-triggered re-synchronization path that produces the same resume point is untested.

The consequence is bounded by the sealed configuration: after the StopSign is accepted no further entries can be accepted, so the phantom decided index carries no value and no value can be mis-assigned; the demonstrated effects are the corrupted index accounting, the unreadable or blank decided log, and the lost reconfiguration endpoint rather than divergent values.

All three nodes used in-memory storage; persistence across a restart and other storages' behaviour on out-of-range reads (a storage-implementer responsibility per the Storage trait) were not exercised.
Only three-node clusters with a single uninterrupted term were exercised; larger clusters and repeated leader changes around the re-synchronization were not.
interpretations.joint_history: Two successive invocations of the same harness lineage, read separately and not combined: receipt 8b314551f1e049fcbf73a358f8ddf2c8 ran the fixed experiment 27bf7fc0875c4342966bd3dc15df80ec-experiment (resync and control cases) and receipt 9125b6a531234e7d9d2fa8cbb817df63 ran its declared successor 3ed5ddd94bce4e94a2dc5b7bb417c18a-experiment (same prefix and cases plus a single-follower case and a read of index 6). Both were produced from the same three-node setup (MemoryStorage, NoSnapshot entries, batch size 1, FIFO delivery without loss) with the same public endpoints; the successor reproduces the resync witness (events 22, 23, 24) and adds the isolated single-replica witness (event 35) and the leader-side hold (event 37). Event index 19 in both receipts is the same pre-resynchronization sampling point.
